# A plain Local job survives SIGKILL of the server. Its durable supervisor
# keeps owning the workload; the restarted server reattaches to the original
# execution, observes its completion and serves its intact logs. The workload
# runs once: ready is created only by its first start.
server start
taskfile release.json release
skygo --json run -f release.json --request-id crash
job-id JOB
await-file ready
await-state $JOB running
server crash
rm ready

server start
await-state $JOB running
! exists ready
mkdir release
await-file released
skygo --json run -f release.json --request-id crash --wait
stdout '"id": *"'$JOB'"'
stdout '"state": *"JOB_STATE_SUCCEEDED"'
skygo jobs logs $JOB
stdout '^first\nsecond\n$'
! exists ready
server stop
! stderr .
